storyContext: GCAM guidance shows that historical context can still be flagged, protective or educational context changes interpretation, and comedy does not automatically erase a harmful meaning. The universal reviewer context layer must therefore distinguish framing modes before judgment.
reasoning: Context analysis must treat framing as meaning-shaping information, not as automatic exemption.
Historical and educational framing are explicit GCAM cues that affect interpretation and confidence.
Comedy, quotation, narration, dream, flashback, documentary style, and scene description are all context signals that the reviewer must evaluate before finalizing a reading.
decision: Store context analysis as a universal reviewer interpretation that distinguishes historical, educational, documentary, comedic, satirical, dream, flashback, quotation, narration, and scene-description framing before legal judgment is made.
alternativeDecisions: Treat every framed line as automatically safe.
Treat every framed line as automatically harmful.
Treat quotation, narration, and scene description as if they were the same thing as direct dialogue.
rejectedInterpretations: Historical context always cancels a finding.
Educational context always cancels a finding.
Quotation is the same as endorsement.
futureReviewNotes: If the repository later exposes a dedicated GCAM documentary, dream, flashback, quotation, narration, or scene-description source, split each into its own source-backed note.
The current GCAM source set explicitly supports historical, educational, and comedy framing observations; the other context modes remain reviewer-methodology framing signals.
